title: How Urban Planning Works
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explore urban planning: the 1950s-era shift to city living (urban population passing rural around May 7), early American city problems, Daniel Burnham's City Beautiful movement and 1906 Plan of Chicago, Roman and Parisian precedents, the goal of urban planning, the physical, social, and economic environments planners consider, master plans, planned communities (Columbia, Maryland; Los Alamos; Oak Ridge), public support and zoning/eminent domain, critiques of planning and the Belt Line in Atlanta, Jane Jacobs' 1961 critique and her five principles (city as ecosystem, bottom-up planning, mixed-use development, varied building ages, density, local economies), gentrification, NASA's rotating wheel space city concept, and Atlanta's sprawl. The episode ends with a listener mail from Andrew in Cleveland about driving to visit his brother in New Orleans with the podcast.
topics: Death and Life of Great American Cities

entities.name: Death and Life of Great American Cities

segments.title: Opening banter and urbanization statistic
segments.summary: Hosts open the show and discuss the day urban population passed rural population, citing researchers' demographic counts and early-1900s urban growth.

segments.title: Early American cities and Burnham's City Beautiful
segments.summary: Describes crowded, poorly built early American cities and Daniel Burnham's City Beautiful program, including his 1893 exposition work and 1906 Plan of Chicago with Edward Bennett.

segments.title: Roman and Parisian precedents
segments.summary: Discusses urban planning roots in Rome (aqueducts, sewers, public spaces) and Louis XIV-era Paris parks that drew settlement, as influences on Burnham.

segments.title: Goal of urban planning and the three environments
segments.summary: Reads the definition of urban planning and explains the physical, social, and economic environments planners consider, including water access and climate.

segments.title: Master plans and feasibility
segments.summary: Explains what a master plan contains, how it is layered in transparency-style pages, and that plans must be feasible with costs and implementation details.

segments.title: Public support, zoning, and eminent domain
segments.summary: Covers the role of public support in planning, a neighborhood group's opposition to a development, zoning laws, and eminent domain, and the Atlanta Belt Line's long timeline.

segments.title: Jane Jacobs and her urban planning principles
segments.summary: Introduces Jane Jacobs and her 1961 book, outlining her ideas: the city as an ecosystem, bottom-up planning, mixed-use development, varied building ages, dense packing, and support for local economies, plus criticism of gentrification.

segments.title: NASA's rotating space city
segments.summary: Describes a NASA-commissioned concept of a rotating wheel city in space that would create gravity, and brief mention of colonizing the Moon and Mars.

segments.title: Atlanta sprawl and transportation
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Atlanta's sprawl, traffic, planned highway widening, and the metro area's size, comparing it to Los Angeles and Phoenix.

segments.title: Listener mail: Andrew's road trip to see his brother
segments.summary: Andrew from Cleveland writes that the podcast kept him awake during an overnight drive to New Orleans to surprise his brother before deployment to Iraq.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode, mention the website search bar and sign off with a brief promo.
